history: Autódromo Internacional Orlando Moura, commonly known as Campo Grande, has been a staple of Brazilian motorsport since its inauguration in 1977. Named after the former governor of Mato Grosso do Sul, the circuit has hosted a variety of national racing series, including Stock Car Brasil, Formula Truck, and various motorcycle championships. The full circuit layout, with its blend of fast straights and technical corners, has been a consistent fixture for these events, providing a challenging test for drivers and riders alike. Over the years, Campo Grande has undergone several upgrades to improve safety and facilities, ensuring its continued relevance in the Brazilian motorsport landscape.
atmosphere: The air crackles with anticipation as the cars line up on the grid at Campo Grande. The roar of the engines echoes off the surrounding hills, creating an intense auditory experience. The vibrant crowd, a mix of seasoned motorsport enthusiasts and families enjoying a day out, adds to the festive atmosphere, their cheers and chants adding an extra layer of excitement. The smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel hangs heavy in the air, a sensory overload that intensifies the thrill of the race.
trackCharacter: The full circuit layout at Campo Grande is a balanced test of power and precision. Its 3.437km length features a mix of long straights where horsepower reigns supreme and a series of tight, technical corners that demand pinpoint accuracy. Drivers must find a rhythm and balance aggression with careful tire management to succeed here. The undulations and subtle camber changes throughout the lap add an extra layer of complexity, rewarding drivers who can adapt to the ever-changing conditions.

famousCorners.name: Curva do S
famousCorners.description: A flowing, high-speed chicane that tests a car's balance and the driver's commitment.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining momentum and carrying speed through the sequence without compromising the exit.

famousCorners.name: Curva da Caixa D'Água
famousCorners.description: A tight, decreasing-radius corner that demands precise braking and throttle control.
famousCorners.challenge: Nailing the apex and avoiding running wide on exit, which can unsettle the car.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Lago
famousCorners.description: A long, sweeping corner with subtle camber changes that tests a car's aerodynamic grip.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining a consistent line and managing tire wear through the extended duration of the turn.

famousCorners.name: Retão Oposto
famousCorners.description: The longest straight on the circuit, offering a crucial overtaking opportunity.
famousCorners.challenge: Maximizing top speed and setting up a clean pass into the subsequent braking zone.

famousCorners.name: Curva da Arquibancada
famousCorners.description: A medium-speed corner right in front of the main grandstand, giving the fans a fantastic view.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining composure and precision with the added pressure of performing in front of the crowd.

keyFactors: Aerodynamic efficiency for the long straights
Braking stability for the tight corners
Tire management, especially rear tire degradation
Adaptability to changing track conditions due to weather
overtakingSpots: Into Curva da Caixa D'Água after the long back straight (Retão Oposto)
Into the first corner (Curva 1) after the start/finish straight
Under braking for Curva do Lago if the car ahead makes a mistake
historySnippets: The circuit is named after former governor Orlando Moura.
It has hosted Stock Car Brasil races for many years.
Formula Truck racing has also been a regular event at Campo Grande.
The circuit is located near the Pantanal, one of the world's largest wetlands.
Campo Grande's layout has remained largely unchanged since its construction.
weatherNotes: Campo Grande experiences a tropical climate with hot and humid conditions for much of the year. Rainfall is common, especially during the summer months (December to February), which can lead to unpredictable track conditions and strategic tire choices. The heat can also take a toll on both drivers and machinery, requiring careful attention to cooling and hydration.
drivingAdvice: Mastering Campo Grande requires a delicate balance between aggression and precision. Conserve tires during the first half of the race, as the abrasive surface can lead to significant degradation. Focus on maximizing exit speed out of the slower corners to carry momentum onto the straights. Be patient in traffic and choose your overtaking opportunities wisely, as the circuit can be challenging to pass on. Setup should prioritize good mechanical grip to deal with the bumpy surface.
famousRaces: Stock Car Brasil race in 2015: A thrilling race with multiple lead changes and a dramatic finish, showcasing the competitive nature of the series.
Formula Truck race in 2010: A chaotic race with several accidents and mechanical failures, highlighting the challenging nature of truck racing on a demanding circuit.
Brazilian Motorcycle Championship round in 2018: A closely contested event with intense battles throughout the field, demonstrating the skill and bravery of the riders.
localCulture: Campo Grande is the capital of Mato Grosso do Sul, a region known for its rich agricultural heritage and vibrant culture. The local cuisine features hearty dishes with beef, rice, and beans as staples. Visitors can explore the nearby Pantanal, a vast wetland teeming with wildlife. The people are warm and welcoming, and motorsport is a popular pastime, creating a passionate and enthusiastic atmosphere at the track. During race weekends, expect to find churrasco (Brazilian barbecue) being served and a festive atmosphere around the circuit.
